question: Once Eisenmenger syndrome has developed in a patient with an uncorrected congenital heart defect, surgical closure of the defect is contraindicated because it would eliminate the right-to-left shunt that acts as a 'pop-off' valve for the right ventricle.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. Surgical closure is absolutely contraindicated in established Eisenmenger syndrome. The shunt, though now causing cyanosis, serves as a pressure relief valve for the right ventricle. Closure would cause fatal right ventricular failure. This is one of the most important management contraindications in adult CHD.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. In Eisenmenger syndrome, pulmonary vascular resistance has risen to equal or exceed systemic resistance, causing reversal of the shunt to right-to-left. Closing the defect at this stage removes the only outlet for the right ventricle, precipitating acute right ventricular failure and death. Management is supportive (pulmonary vasodilators: sildenafil, bosentan; avoiding vasodilators, dehydration, iron deficiency).
